_what_this_is: THE BASIC TIER. A person on a road, in or near a vehicle that cannot move. They are not lost - they know exactly where they are. This is the half this pack's own planning notes call 'the half that earns the pack its place': most Canadians meet this several times in a life, and the published guidance is the clearest and least ambiguous of anything in this pack. Every action below is VERIFIED and, unless stated otherwise, UNANIMOUS across the sources named in citations.json.
_zero_signal: Every action below is static text with no field a model can rewrite. It works with the phone in a drawer.
title_en: Stranded in a vehicle, in a storm or on a back road
who_this_is_for_en: You are in or near a vehicle that cannot move. You know where you are.

actions.text_en: Stay in the vehicle. In blowing snow you can lose sight of it within moments of leaving it, and become impossible to find.
Clear the exhaust pipe of snow and ice, and check it again from time to time. A blocked pipe pushes carbon monoxide back into the vehicle.
If you run the engine, open a window slightly for fresh air, for the same reason.

Run the engine only in short stretches for heat, not continuously. One source publishes about ten minutes each hour; another says only occasionally, with no number. If you want a figure to use, use ten minutes an hour - and know that is not agreed doctrine, it is one source's number among sources that disagree.
Tie something bright to the antenna, or hang it from a window. Once snow stops falling, raise the hood.
Move your arms, legs, fingers and toes to keep blood moving. Do not overexert yourself - sweating in the cold works against you.

Keep your phone charged - a vehicle can recharge it - and call 911 if you have any signal at all. An emergency call connects through any carrier's tower in range, even if you have no active plan with that carrier.
actions.note_en: This is the vehicle answer and it is the opposite of the on-foot answer this pack gives elsewhere - see bush_lost.json's phone section. A vehicle has an alternator and, per the sourced guidance, a charging cable is part of the recommended kit; a person on foot has neither, which is why the two scenarios are not given the same phone instruction.

withheld_from_this_scenario.text_en: This pack does not compare building a snow shelter against staying in the vehicle beyond telling you to stay in the vehicle (action 1). A search and rescue partner has not confirmed the comparison, so this pack does not go further than the one instruction it can source unconditionally.
